object_entity.proposition_label: The gospel reached India through early missionary or apostolic activity
object_entity.description: Christianity reached India — whether the Malabar coast or the broader "India" of ancient usage — through apostolic (Thomas, Bartholomew) or early missionary (Pantaenus) activity; attested by Eusebius HE 5.10 and Philostorgius.

passage.excerpt: A man named Pantaenus was put in charge of the catechetical school at Alexandria, a school whose existence is attested from ancient times. This man had been trained in the Stoic system of philosophy; tradition reports he went as far as India to preach Christ to the Brahmans. Clement of Alexandria names him in his own writings as his instructor, showing that Pantaenus stood in the succession of teachers at Alexandria.
